source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Clutch and Transmissions, p.7-40

procedures.title: Turbo Hydra-Matic oil leak diagnosis
steps: Front end (continued): check the pump O-ring and also the pump groove and case bore; check for a porous pump or case.

Oil from the vent pipe: look for overfilling, water in the oil, a misplaced pump to case gasket, dirt between pump and case or between pump cover and body, a porous case or badly machined pump face, or a pump short of stock on its mounting faces or porous.

procedures.title: Turbo Hydra-Matic case porosity repair
steps: Road test to bring the transmission to operating temperature.
Raise the car and, with the engine running, find the leak, checking every selector position; a mirror helps.
Stop the engine, clean the area well with solvent and blow it dry.
Mix enough epoxy cement, part #1360016, following the maker's directions.
While the case is still hot, cover the leak area completely with epoxy.
Let it cure three hours, then retest as in the first two steps.

procedures.title: Turbo Hydra-Matic oil pressure check (car stationary)
steps: Hook up the pressure gauge and a tachometer.
With the modulator vacuum tube disconnected, zero output speed and the engine at 1200 rpm, compare readings with the altitude table.
With the vacuum tube connected and the engine at about 600-800 rpm, compare with the second set of values.

specs.what: pressure, tube off, 1200 rpm, 0 ft: Drive/Neutral/Park | L1 or L2 | Reverse
pressure, tube connected, 600-800 rpm: Drive/Neutral/Park | L1 or L2 | Reverse

notes: Altitude and barometric pressure have little effect on the readings with the vacuum tube connected.
Units are not printed in the table (pressures in psi).

procedures.title: Turbo Hydra-Matic vacuum modulator checks
steps: Diaphragm leak: push a pipe cleaner as far as it goes into the vacuum connector pipe; transmission oil on it means replace the modulator.

Atmospheric leak: brush soap solution over the vacuum pipe seam, the crimped upper-to-lower housing seam and the threaded screw seal; blow into the vacuum pipe through a short rubber tube and replace the modulator if bubbles appear.
Bellows comparison: put a known good modulator on one end of the comparison gauge and the suspect one on the other.
Hold them level and push them together until one sleeve end just reaches the center line of the gauge.

specs.what: max air pressure for atmospheric leak test

specs.value: 13/32" to 3/8" round or flat stock, ends square within 1/64"

notes: Over 50% of modulators returned as faulty were found good, so test before replacing.
Gasoline or water vapor alone (no oil) on the vacuum side is not a reason to replace.
Use only breath to pressurize; more than 6 psi can damage the modulator.
The comparison gauge is shown in figure 6T in the manual (overall 1" long with a scribed line at 1/2").
